newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares seen quiet in holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares seen quiet in holiday mood.

text.p: Brazil's stock market is seen quiet Monday as today's holidays in the U.S. and Britain and a slow week in Brasilia are likely to keep investors on the sidelines, brokers said.
"Today is likely to be pretty much quiet. There is nothing to look forward to," said a senior trader, adding that the bolsa's turnover is expected to shrink.
Brazil's Congress is taking this week off, leaving a second round vote on a re-election bill and further voting on amendments to a civil service reform until at least June 4.
Thursday is the Corpus Cristi holiday, which made it impractical to schedule ballots.
Also, key government ministers are abroad, which will probably help weakening newspaper headlines this week, traders said.

Traders expect trading in Banespa to resume today after a three-day suspension. Last week Sao Paulo state and the federal government signed a final debt rescheduling deal under which Banespa will be transferred to federal hands.
